assessment.nobel_worthiness: The acoustic-peak structure of the CMB and its precision mapping turned cosmology into a quantitative science, fixing the geometry, baryon and dark-matter content and the initial conditions of structure formation. It is a discovery at the centre in the sense of my own committee practice: a measurement that nature supplied and many later results rest on. The impact is lasting and very clear.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over experimental and theoretical lines (COBE-era anisotropies, balloon and ground experiments, WMAP, Planck). The list names five people; a fair three-person configuration would plausibly favour the WMAP leadership and the key precision analysis, but this omits Planck (Puget) and the early theory of acoustic oscillations (Sunyaev). That is a real allocation problem, and I cannot verify the finer history of who decided what.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently and repeatedly by several experiments over more than two decades, with a very stable interpretation in the standard cosmological model. Recognition is fully mature, arguably overdue relative to the earlier COBE and cosmology prizes, although the earlier prizes narrow what is left to credit.
uncertainties: Whether the prize can fairly omit Planck/HFI and Sunyaev's theoretical contribution.
How to separate the acoustic-peak discovery from the broader parameter-measurement program and from earlier recognised CMB work.
Tensions such as the Hubble constant do not undermine the discovery but may be raised against its completeness.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combines the magic-wavelength idea with ultracold strontium atoms to reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, far past the microwave cesium standard. It opens redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants and dark-sector physics. A clear invention with a clear experimental payoff.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the early realisation; Ye's group drove the record-setting performance and many-body clock developments. The two-person configuration is natural and the list supports it. Other groups (e.g. ion clocks, Hall and Hänsch precedents) are already recognised or distinct.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many laboratories worldwide, stable and mature, with ongoing progress towards a redefinition of the SI second. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as overlapping with prior frequency-comb and ion-clock prizes.
Whether others (e.g. contributors to the strontium cooling and lattice-spectroscopy lines) deserve more credit than the two-name list suggests.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, later supported by identification of a flaring blazar and the Galactic plane signal, opened neutrino astronomy at energies far beyond earlier prizes. It is a discovery made by nature and delivered by an instrument built for that purpose, with large impact on multi-messenger astrophysics.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and Karle was central to the detector and the analysis, so the supplied pair is credible. A very large collaboration and other leaders (for instance the broader project leadership) mean the allocation is a judgment I cannot fully verify from the list.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is established at high significance and independently confirmed. Source identification is still developing, but the discovery of the flux itself is mature enough. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: The count of source associations is still limited, so the astrophysical interpretation remains incomplete.
Whether a prize should recognise the project leadership, the instrument builders or the analysis team that made the first-detection claim.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical proposal for quantum logic gates with trapped ions and the experimental realisation of ion-based quantum registers laid the foundation for a leading quantum-computing platform. Importance and originality are high, and the line from proposal to working gates is unusually clear.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the decisive 1995 proposal; experimental demonstrations came from several groups, with Blatt's Innsbruck group prominent in scalable entanglement and algorithms. Wineland and Haroche were recognised in 2012, which makes the experimental credit allocation delicate. The theory-plus-experiment configuration is fair but not unambiguous.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature as a platform with independent confirmation by many groups, though large-scale quantum computing remains incomplete. The recent recognition of other quantum-technology work may affect timing.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize for ion manipulation.
Whether an experimentalist such as Blatt or others (e.g. Monroe, Wineland-line contributors) is the right third laureate.
Cirac and Zoller are also credited elsewhere on the list, so credit between candidate packages is entangled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, followed by the experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, created a whole field of topological phases with surfaces protected by time-reversal symmetry. The concept is original and widely influential and extends the earlier topological-phase prize.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele are the clear theorists. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted HgTe and are not on the supplied list, and Molenkamp's group made the observation. Fu, Kane and 3D topological insulator work is also separate. A fair prize needs a careful statement of what is rewarded, and the supplied names support a plausible theory-plus-experiment trio.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently in several materials, with a stable interpretation. Technological payoff is still limited but the scientific recognition is mature.
uncertainties: Absent credit for Zhang and collaborators in the HgTe prediction, which are not in the supplied names.
Overlap with the 2016 Thouless, Haldane, Kosterlitz prize for topological phases.
The compound discovery spans 2D and 3D insulators that may deserve different attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at magic twist angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened twistronics and a large body of moire physics. The combination of prediction and confirmation is strong and original.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key continuum-model prediction and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery. The three-name configuration is natural. Other experimental groups (e.g. Dean, Young) and earlier theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) could be argued for, so some credit is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Replicated widely within a few years, but the origin of superconductivity and correlated states is still debated. The field is young, so recognition may be somewhat early, although the discovery itself is solid.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity remains unsettled.
Earlier theoretical antecedents may challenge the sole claim of the proposed theorists.
Whether it is premature compared with older candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* are direct, striking observational evidence of black-hole shadows and a test of strong-field gravity, which touches my own field of gravitation. The scientific impact is high, while the specific quantitative constraints on alternatives to black holes are still modest.
assessment.attribution: The EHT is a collaboration of hundreds, with Doeleman as the director of the project, Falcke as the proposer of the shadow imaging idea and Zensus on the European VLBI side. A three-person selection is hard to defend without much more detail, and I cannot independently verify the internal division of credit.
assessment.maturity: M87* and Sgr A* results have been consistent with general relativity and have had follow-up polarisation work, but independent confirmation by a separate instrument is limited. This is mature enough for recognition but the interpretation of images, and what they constrain, is still evolving.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale attribution and the three-person limit.
Limited independent confirmation outside the EHT collaboration.
Gravitational-physics constraints are modest relative to the imaging achievement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The AdS/CFT correspondence reshaped quantum gravity, strongly coupled field theory and black-hole physics, and it is among the most cited ideas in high-energy theory. Its conceptual importance is very large. As a theorist in this area I am also conscious that its direct contact with nature is limited.
assessment.attribution: Maldacena made the original conjecture, with Gubser-Klebanov-Polyakov and Witten giving the dictionary. Susskind and 't Hooft are linked to the holographic principle. The supplied four names have no unique three-person subset, so I choose the ones closest to the formulation, accepting that this is contestable.
assessment.maturity: There is a great deal of mathematical and computational evidence and many applications, but it is not an experimentally verified statement about our universe. Whether a prize is timely depends on the committee's willingness to reward a theory without direct observational test.
uncertainties: Lack of direct empirical confirmation in nature.
Contested allocation among Maldacena, Gubser, Klebanov, Polyakov, Witten, Susskind and others not all in the list.
Applications to condensed matter and QCD plasma are suggestive rather than decisive.
